documents.title: Sample AI Policy Language
documents.summary: The Teaching & Learning Center asks instructors to add an AI statement to the syllabus and offers three sets of model wording: prohibited, permitted and required. Each ties unattributed AI use to the K-State Honor Pledge, and the permitted and required versions give a citation format. The page is sample language, not a binding rule.
documents.stance_why: The page says "Please add language to your syllabus regarding your policies toward AI tools" and supplies templates headed "AI Prohibited", "AI Permitted" and "AI Required", so the university sets no stance itself and leaves the choice to instructors with tiers listed.

units.why: The template page tells instructors to put an AI policy in the syllabus: "Please add language to your syllabus regarding your policies toward AI tools." This is a syllabus-statement expectation addressed to instructors (P09), set before the course.
units.anchor: Please add language to your syllabus regarding your policies toward AI tools

units.why: "This course assumes that all your course work will be done by you" says submitted work must be the student's own, which is P29 (own what you submit), not a ban by itself.
units.anchor: This course assumes that all your course work will be done by you.

units.why: "You will not need to use artificial intelligence (AI) tools" signals AI is not expected but does not forbid it; the following sentences supply the narrower ban, so this is P03 (discourage without forbidding).
units.anchor: You will not need to use artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT
units.policy: Students will not need to use AI tools such as ChatGPT for any of the assignments.

units.why: "you should not have an AI instrument do the writing of any portion of any assignment" bars having AI produce submitted work, which is P19; it is phrased as should-not, hence that modality.
units.anchor: you should not have an AI instrument do the writing of any portion

units.why: The analogy "just as you would not have another person do your writing for you" frames AI like a human helper under ordinary authorship rules, which is P45 rather than P19 because it explains the ban by analogy.
units.anchor: just as you would not have another person do your writing for you

units.why: "My aim is to keep the focus on your originality and creativity, your learning and reflection" gives the learning reason for the limit; P41 (doing the work yourself builds skill) fits best.
units.anchor: My aim is to keep the focus on your originality and creativity

units.why: Even in the prohibited template, "you will need to cite it fully and properly" requires citation of any AI use, a disclosure duty (P24).
units.anchor: you will need to cite it fully and properly

units.why: The prohibited template names an external style, "MLA's AI citation guidelines", as the required format for AI citations, so it specifies how to cite (P25) rather than only that one must cite.
units.anchor: using MLA's AI citation guidelines
units.policy: Students cite AI use using MLA's AI citation guidelines.

units.why: "Using an AI tool to generate assignment content without proper attribution would be a violation of the K-State Honor Pledge" makes unattributed AI use the violation, so P28 (nondisclosure is the violation) fits better than the generic P36. It is repeated in each template and coded once.
units.anchor: Using an AI tool to generate assignment content without proper attribution would be a violation
units.policy: Using an AI tool to generate assignment content without proper attribution would be a violation of the K-State Honor Pledge.

units.why: "You may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to assist your learning in this course" sets a default of permitted use, P02.
units.anchor: You may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to assist your learning in this course

units.why: The permitted template lists "idea generation" as an allowed use, which is brainstorming (P15).
units.anchor: including idea generation
units.policy: AI tools may be used for idea generation for written assignments.

units.why: "grammar assessments for written assignments" allows AI for grammar checking of prose, a prose-specific use that belongs in P18 (prose separate from code).
units.anchor: grammar assessments for written assignments
units.policy: AI tools may be used for grammar assessments of written assignments.

units.why: "you are prohibited from using generative AI tools to completely produce, reproduce, and/or manufacture paper" forbids having AI make the submitted work, P19, while leaving other uses open.
units.anchor: you are prohibited from using generative AI tools to completely produce, reproduce, and/or manufacture paper

units.why: "you are expected to provide a citation for it" requires citing appropriate AI use, a disclosure duty (P24).
units.anchor: you are expected to provide a citation for it

units.why: The format "Prompt or brief description of topic of search depending on tool. Date of creation." requires the tool, the prompt and a date, matching P25.
units.anchor: Prompt or brief description of topic of search depending on tool. Date of creation.
units.policy: Citations of AI use give the title of the AI tool, the prompt or a brief description of the topic of search, and the date of creation.

units.why: "It is your responsibility, however, to be transparent in your AI use" places a disclosure duty on the student (P24).
units.anchor: It is your responsibility, however, to be transparent in your AI use.

units.why: "you are required to read and edit, thoroughly, your assignment submissions, particularly any items created using AI" makes students answerable for what they submit; P29 fits better than P31 because wrongness of AI output is not stated here.
units.anchor: you are required to read and edit, thoroughly, your assignment submissions

units.why: "you will include a 150-300 word AI Acknowledgement" requires a statement with every submission, P24.
units.anchor: you will include a 150-300 word AI Acknowledgement

units.why: Component one, "A citation for the tool/s used" with the prompt and date format, is a P25 specification of what the citation contains.
units.anchor: A citation for the tool/s used
units.policy: The AI Acknowledgement includes a citation for the tool or tools used, in the format "Title of AI Tool. Prompt or brief description of topic of search depending on tool. Date of creation."

units.why: "An explanation of why you decided to use the tool(s)" is a required written reflection on AI use, P26 (reflections).
units.anchor: An explanation of why you decided to use the tool(s)

units.why: "A description of how you used the tool(s) to manage assignment requirements" is a required account of the AI use, P26.
units.anchor: A description of how you used the tool(s) to manage assignment requirements.

units.why: "A reflection on your experience using the tool, exploring what worked or didn't, and acknowledging limitations of the tool" is a required reflection (P26); the mention of "potential biases" is secondary so P53 is not used.
units.anchor: A reflection on your experience using the tool, exploring what worked or didn't

units.why: "This course encourages and embraces the ethical use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)" sets a default of encouraging AI, P02.
units.anchor: This course encourages and embraces the ethical use of Artificial Intelligence (AI).

units.why: "you will sometimes be required to incorporate AI tools in your work" builds AI into the coursework, which is the require stance; P02 (expect AI use) is the nearest type.
units.anchor: you will sometimes be required to incorporate AI tools in your work

units.why: "develop our understanding of this technology ... both as students and future professionals" gives a career and learning reason for required use, P44.
units.anchor: both as students and future professionals

units.why: "we will be transparent in our use of AI in the completion of any classroom tasks" commits to openness about AI use, a disclosure duty (P24), tied to Student Code of Conduct integrity rules.
units.anchor: we will be transparent in our use of AI

units.why: "you should cite AI tools as follows" gives the citation format in the required-use template, P25.
units.anchor: you should cite AI tools as follows
units.policy: Students should cite AI tools in the format "Title of AI Tool. Prompt or brief description of topic of search depending on tool. Date of creation."

units.why: "the policies around the use of large language tools vary across courses" says rules differ by course, P11 (each course's policy governs only that course).
units.anchor: the policies around the use of large language tools vary across courses
units.policy: Policies around the use of large language tools vary across courses.

units.why: "we will spend some time early in the semester co-creating a class agreement on the use of AI tools" has the class set its own rule, closest to P04 (rule set per course or activity rather than one fixed rule).
units.anchor: we will spend some time early in the semester co-creating a class agreement
units.frag_end: academic integrity in the Student Code of Conduct,

units.why: In the second required-use version, "we will be transparent in our use of AI in the completion of any classroom tasks" is a separate transparency commitment (P24).
units.anchor: we will be transparent in our use of AI
units.frag_start: In our development, we will follow

documents.title: Using Generative AI with University Owned Records and Data Policy
documents.date_or_term: current (accessed 2026-10-25); date not stated in extracted text
documents.summary: An unnumbered draft policy on how employees and contractors may use generative AI with university records and data. It allows use with human review and disclosure, bars entering Protected Information (including student coursework and grades) into unapproved tools, and lists sanctions. It does not govern student coursework.
documents.stance_why: The policy says use "is dependent on the specific use" and that users "must exercise good and sound judgment", then lists restricted uses ("The University restricts the following uses"); AI is allowed with conditions, so permit rather than restrict. It is a draft for employees.

units.why: The statement "To comply with the State of Kansas Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy and to mitigate risk" sets the purpose and authority of an institutional framework for AI use by employees, P56.
units.anchor: To comply with the State of Kansas Generative Artificial Intelligence Policy

units.why: "intended to mitigate the following risks to the University" with malware, loss of IP and reputational damage states the policy's rationale; it is coded P56 because it is a purpose statement.
units.anchor: intended to mitigate the following risks to the University

units.why: "The purpose of this Policy is to regulate the use of Generative AI with University-owned records and data within the employment sector" defines the policy's scope as employment and records, not coursework, P56.
units.anchor: The purpose of this Policy is to regulate the use of Generative AI

units.why: "This Policy emphasizes the need for annual updates" commits to regular revision, P54.
units.anchor: This Policy emphasizes the need for annual updates

units.why: "oversees the annual review, updating, and implementation of the policy" assigns offices to maintain the policy on a yearly cycle (P54).
units.anchor: oversees the annual review, updating, and implementation of the policy
units.frag_start: This policy falls under the authority

units.why: "This Policy applies to all employees of the University and service providers and contractors" fixes who is bound; it defines scope (P56) and does not cover students as users.
units.anchor: This Policy applies to all employees of the University and service providers and contractors
units.frag_start: This Policy applies to all employees

units.why: "This Policy applies to all business use cases" including software code, correspondence, institutional research, admissions and student publications defines the scope of covered uses (P56).
units.anchor: This Policy applies to all business use cases involving the University
units.frag_start: This Policy applies to all business

units.why: "use of Generative AI for personal reasons should not occur on University-issued devices" limits personal AI use on university equipment; the closest type is P50 (protect data, use vetted channels).
units.anchor: use of Generative AI for personal reasons should not occur on University-issued devices
units.policy: Use of Generative AI for personal reasons should not occur on University-issued devices and should not use, rely on, or be populated with the University's records or data.

units.why: "Whether users should use Generative AI in the performance of their responsibilities is dependent on the specific use" makes the choice depend on the task, P04 (decided per activity).
units.anchor: dependent on the specific use of Generative AI

units.why: "Users must exercise good and sound judgment" before using AI, an individual duty of care that fits P04 (judgment per use) better than the accountability types, which address students.
units.anchor: Users must exercise good and sound judgment

units.why: "shall be reviewed by knowledgeable human operators for accuracy, appropriateness, legality, privacy, and security" requires checking AI output before use, P31.
units.anchor: reviewed by knowledgeable human operators for accuracy, appropriateness, legality, privacy, and security

units.why: AI use "may create University records that fall under the Kansas Opens Record Act" is a records-law consequence of AI use that no type covers.
units.anchor: may create University records that fall under the Kansas Opens Record Act
units.uncovered_note: AI outputs may be public records under the state open-records act; records-law obligations for AI use.

units.why: "Employees shall ensure that service providers and contractors align with the University's principles on the ethical use of AI" governs vendor conduct, P65.
units.anchor: Employees shall ensure that service providers and contractors align with the University's principles
units.frag_end: comply with relevant legal regulations (including the GDPR and FERPA).

units.why: Vendors "must disclose in their contracts with the University that their tools incorporate Generative AI", a vendor-agreement requirement, P65.
units.anchor: must disclose in their contracts with the University that their tools incorporate Generative AI

units.why: Vendors handling KSU data "are required to obtain pre-approval from the Data Governance Steward Committee", a review step for vendor AI use, P65.
units.anchor: Furthermore, they are required to obtain

units.why: "The University firmly restricts the use of unaligned or intentionally misaligned Generative AI models", defined as platforms without a university contract, steers use to vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: The University firmly restricts the use of unaligned or intentionally misaligned Generative AI models
units.frag_start: The University firmly restricts the use

units.why: "Prior approval from the Data Governance Steward Committee ... is required for any proposed utilization of an unaligned AI model" sets an exception route, P50.
units.anchor: Prior approval from the Data Governance Steward Committee

units.why: "The use of Generative AI may not breach the University's obligations to comply with applicable state and federal laws" sets a legal-compliance principle, a framework statement (P56).
units.anchor: may not breach the University's obligations to comply with applicable state and federal laws

units.why: "Users shall not enter any Protected Information into Generative AI that is not an approved process or system" protects confidential data, P50.
units.anchor: Users shall not enter any Protected Information into Generative AI

units.why: The restriction on "Materials that go against Copyright and Artificial Intelligence" laws and university policy concerns copyright of AI inputs and outputs, P52.
units.anchor: Materials that go against Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
units.policy: The University restricts materials that go against Copyright and Artificial Intelligence laws and Intellectual Property laws and University policies.

units.why: "Users shall not use Generative AI to generate or enable content that is discriminatory, defamatory, illegal" bans harmful output, P53.
units.anchor: Users shall not use Generative AI to generate or enable content that is discriminatory, defamatory

units.why: Banning upload of data "that could be used to help create or carry out malware, spam and phishing campaigns" is a cybersecurity misuse rule with no matching type.
units.anchor: Users shall not use Generative AI to upload any data that could be used
units.uncovered_note: Ban on using generative AI for malware, spam, phishing or cyber scams.

units.why: AI responses "shall not ... be assumed to be truthful, credible, or accurate"; this is the verify-output idea, P31.
units.anchor: be assumed to be truthful, credible, or accurate
units.frag_start: Responses generated from Generative AI shall not:

units.why: AI responses "shall not ... be used verbatim" requires people not to pass AI text on unchanged; P32 (AI must not replace one's own thinking) is closer than P19, which is about students.
units.anchor: be used verbatim
units.frag_start: Responses generated from Generative AI shall not:

units.why: AI responses "shall not ... be used to issue official statements (i.e., policy, legislation, or regulations)" bars AI for official statements; no type covers this institutional-communication rule.
units.anchor: be used to issue official statements
units.frag_start: Responses generated from Generative AI shall not:
units.uncovered_note: No AI-issued official statements (policy, legislation, regulation).

units.why: AI responses "shall not ... be used to break the University's Principles of Community" ties AI use to community values, closest to P53 (harms).
units.anchor: be used to break the University's Principles of Community
units.frag_start: Responses generated from Generative AI shall not:

units.why: "Persons violating this Policy may be held personally liable for resulting damages and civil or criminal charges" states consequences in advance, P37.
units.anchor: Persons violating this Policy may be held personally liable

units.why: "employees who fail to follow it may be subject to sanctions ... including written reprimand and in serious cases, termination for cause" lists penalties, P37.
units.anchor: written reprimand and in serious cases, termination for cause

units.why: "its use should be disclosed and made clear on the document" asks that AI-assisted documents carry a disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: its use should be disclosed and made clear on the document

units.why: The definition "A form of artificial intelligence that utilizes algorithms and models trained on large datasets to generate new creative content" fixes what the policy covers, P61.
units.anchor: A form of artificial intelligence that utilizes algorithms and models trained on large datasets

units.why: The Protected Information definition lists "Coursework produced by students" and student grades as FERPA data that may not be entered into AI, which makes this data protection (P50) relevant to teaching.
units.anchor: Coursework produced by students
units.frag_start: Personally identifiable information protected by FERPA
units.policy: Protected Information includes personally identifiable information protected by FERPA, such as coursework produced by students, student grades, student disability information and student disciplinary records.

units.why: The definition of "Unaligned" as "A Generative AI platform lacking a contractual agreement or vendor status with the University" sets the meaning of the restricted category, P61.
units.anchor: A Generative AI platform lacking a contractual agreement or vendor status

units.why: "The University reserves the right to audit networks and systems periodically to ensure compliance" is a monitoring mechanism, P40.
units.anchor: reserves the right to audit networks and systems periodically to ensure compliance

units.why: "All breaches of information security, actual or suspected, must be reported to and investigated by the Director of Information Security" is a reporting duty not covered by a type.
units.anchor: All breaches of information security, actual or suspected, must be reported
units.uncovered_note: Duty to report suspected information-security breaches to the security director.

units.why: "subject to disciplinary action up to and including loss of computer access" states consequences for violating security rules, P37.
units.anchor: subject to disciplinary action up to and including loss of computer access

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (Responsible Use of Generative AI Task Force)
documents.summary: The Provost's page describes a task force charged with building a university AI framework covering academic integrity, data, procurement and AI literacy. It states no rules for students or instructors; the policies are still to be developed.
documents.stance_why: The page says the task force "is charged with developing and evolving university policy" and sets no rule itself, so no stance is stated; delegates is the closest option since decisions rest with future policy and current instructors.

units.why: "A thoughtful and strategic framework is needed to ensure these technologies are used in ways that align with the university's vision" says an institution-level framework is needed, P56.
units.anchor: A thoughtful and strategic framework is needed

units.why: The task force "has been charged to develop a comprehensive institutional strategic framework with policies, procedures, training and educational services", an institution-wide framework in progress, P56.
units.anchor: charged to develop a comprehensive institutional strategic framework
units.frag_start: A University Task Force on Responsible

units.why: The task force is to develop "and evolving university policy, guidelines, and training", so the policy is acknowledged as ongoing work, P54.
units.anchor: developing and evolving university policy, guidelines, and training and support services

units.why: The focus area "Academic Integrity and Ethical Use" shows student-facing integrity rules are planned but not yet stated; P56 as a scope statement.
units.anchor: Academic Integrity and Ethical Use

units.why: "Protection of Unpublished Research, Confidential and Clinical Data, and IP" is a planned data-protection area, P50.
units.anchor: Protection of Unpublished Research, Confidential and Clinical Data, and IP

units.why: "Procurement Process and Vetting by IT" plans review of AI tools before acquisition, P65.
units.anchor: Procurement Process and Vetting by IT

units.why: "How are we defining generative AI, agentic AI, etc." lists defining AI terms as a task, P61.
units.anchor: How are we defining generative AI, agentic AI, etc.

units.why: The task force will "Review strategies, policies and practices related to AI use ... including those at peer institutions"; this is benchmarking for later revision, nearest P54.
units.anchor: Review strategies, policies and practices related to AI use and expanding AI literacy

units.why: "Define principles for responsible and ethical use of generative AI" is a task to set a framework, P56.
units.anchor: Define principles for responsible and ethical use of generative AI

units.why: The task force will "Develop recommendations for a set of policies or guidelines to govern the use of AI by students, faculty, researchers and staff", an institution-wide policy still to come, P56.
units.anchor: Develop recommendations for a set of policies or guidelines to govern the use of AI

units.why: "Recommend ongoing governance structures to monitor and update policies as necessary" commits to later revision, P54.
units.anchor: Recommend ongoing governance structures to monitor and update policies as necessary.

units.why: "integrate AI education/literacy, training and support services into academic programs, faculty development initiatives" plans AI literacy for students and faculty; P44 (teach AI use as a skill) is chosen over P63 because academic programs come first.
units.anchor: integrate AI education/literacy, training and support services into academic programs

units.why: "Develop Research Recommendations" lists research use of AI as a planned area, P62.
units.anchor: Develop Research Recommendations

units.why: "Make sure IP issues and issues around course content created by faculty and IP research are clearly addressed" plans IP guidance on course content, P52.
units.anchor: Make sure IP issues and issues around course content created by faculty

units.why: The roadmap will set "a timeline for developing and implementing an integrated set of AI-related policies and practices", a plan for future policy, P54.
units.anchor: a timeline for developing and implementing an integrated set of AI-related policies and practices
units.frag_start: Identify the key milestones, a timeline

notes: Coder B. K-State has no adopted student-facing AI rule in the collected texts; the TLC page offers templates, the records document is an employee draft (Chapter ????), the provost page is a task force description. Uncovered: open-records consequence, malware/phishing ban, official statements ban, breach reporting.
